subtitle: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and the Vadda Ghallughara: a nation walks through fire

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a vast caravan under a darkening sky, warriors forming a ring around distant carts
panels.action: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia stands in the foreground on horseback, grim and resolute, while behind him stretches an endless line of wagons and walking families crossing the dusty plains of Punjab as ominous dust clouds rise on the horizon.

dialogue.text: February 1762, the plains of Punjab: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia rides with a people on the move, as Ahmad Shah Durrani closes in to crush the Sikhs in what will be remembered as the Vadda Ghallughara.

i18n.hi: फ़रवरी 1762, पंजाब के मैदान: जੱਸा सिंह अहलूवालिया चलते काफ़िले संग सवार, जबकि अहमद शाह दुर्रानी सिक्खों को कुचलने पास आता है — जिसे वड्डा ਘੱਲूਘਾਰਾ कहा जाएगा।

panels.shot: high aerial wide over the Sutlej-Yamuna Doab, rivers and fields under winter haze
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows the wintry landscape of central Punjab, scattered villages, bare trees, and distant fort-like towns as faint columns of smoke rise in different directions.

dialogue.text: A decade after the fall of the Mughals, the Punjab is a broken chessboard. Between the Sutlej and the Ravi, Afghan raids, Mughal remnants and Sikh misls tug and tear at the land.

i18n.hi: मुग़लों के पतन के दस साल बाद, पंजाब टूटी बिसात है। सतलज से रावी तक अफ़ग़ान धावे, मुग़ल अवशेष और सिख मिसलें मिलकर ज़मीन को नोच रही हैं।

panels.shot: mid-wide of Afghan cavalry column in winter light, seen from behind
panels.action: Armoured Afghan horsemen ride in a long disciplined column along a dusty track, tall standards fluttering, a compact core of artillery carts creaking in the center.

dialogue.text: From the northwest rides Ahmad Shah Durrani, the Abdali. After Panipat he returns again and again, seeking to hold Delhi in fear and to stamp out this new Sikh power rising from village and forest.

i18n.hi: उत्तर–पश्चिम से अहमद शाह दुर्रानी, अबदाली, फिर चढ़ता है। पानीपत के बाद वो बार–बार लौटता है, दिल्ली को डर में रखने और गाँव–जंगल से उठती नई सिख ताक़त को कुचलने।

panels.shot: close-up on Jassa Singh’s weathered face, eyes intent, faint dust on his beard
panels.action: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia’s face fills the frame, lined yet unbent, his gaze steady as he looks past the viewer toward some distant threat, a steel helmet resting in the crook of his arm.

dialogue.text: At the heart of that rising stands Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, chosen earlier by the Sarbat Khalsa as leader of the Dal Khalsa, a raiding confederacy grown into a people’s shield.

i18n.hi: उस उभार के केंद्र में जੱਸा सिंह अहलूवालिया खड़े हैं, जिन्हें सरबत ख़ालसा ने दल ख़ालसा का सरदार चुना था — लुटारे दल से बनी एक कौम की ढाल।

panels.shot: wide of a massive moving caravan, camera tracking alongside
panels.action: The frame shows an immense Sikh vahir—wagons, pack animals, women carrying bundles, elders on carts, children clinging to ropes—moving slowly, while Jassa Singh rides along the flank, issuing calm orders to scattered warriors.

dialogue.text: In early 1762 the Sikhs are not in pitched battle array. They are on the move as a whole community, a vahir of misldars, families and grain, shifting their base with the season.

i18n.hi: 1762 की शुरुआत में सिख कोई जंगी क़तार में नहीं। पूरा कौम एक साथ चल रहा है — मिसलदार, परिवार और अनाज की वाहिर, मौसम के साथ ठिकाना बदलती।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jassa Singh in council with other unseen chiefs, campfire light on his face
panels.action: Jassa Singh stands beside a small roadside fire at dusk, gesturing toward a rough map scratched in the dust as the silhouettes of other Sikh chiefs lean in, listening intently.

dialogue.text: Near Barnala and Malerkotla the misls weigh their choices. Afghan forces sweep in from the west. Mughal-allied chiefs watch from their forts. The Sikh counsel is simple: keep the people together, keep moving.

i18n.hi: बरनाला और मलेरकोटला के पास मिसलें अपना रास्ता तौलती हैं। पश्चिम से अफ़ग़ान फ़ौजें झाड़ू की तरह बढ़ती हैं। मुग़ल–परस्त सरदार क़िलों से ताकते हैं। सिख मशविरा साफ़ है: कौम को साथ रखो, चलते रहो।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle wide of Afghan scouts spotting the caravan from a ridge
panels.action: On a scrubby ridge, Afghan scouts draw up their horses, pointing their spears towards the distant dust plume of the Sikh vahir, their faces lit with sudden, sharp excitement.

dialogue.text: Yet movement cannot hide such a host. Afghan scouts sight the slow river of people near Kup and Rahira, and word gallops back to Ahmad Shah of a chance for a crushing blow.

i18n.hi: पर इतनी भीड़ को चलना छुपा नहीं सकता। कूप और रहीरा के पास धीमी चलती इस नदी को अफ़ग़ान जासूस देख लेते हैं, और अहमद शाह तक खबर पहुंचती है कि घातक वार का मौका है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Abdali’s army forming a crescent, seen from behind their lines
panels.action: A vast Afghan force fans out across open ground, cavalry spreading into a crescent, matchlockmen taking positions, camel-mounted guns being hauled forward under the winter sun.

dialogue.text: Contemporary Afghan accounts tell us his army swings wide to encircle. This is not a border raid. It is a planned encirclement, a noose cast around a moving nation.

i18n.hi: उसी ज़माने के अफ़ग़ान बयान बताते हैं, उसकी फ़ौज घेरने को चौड़ा चक्कर काटती है। ये कोई सरहदी धावा नहीं, ये सोची–समझी घेराबंदी है — चलते क़ौम पर डाली फांसी की रस्सी।

panels.shot: tight medium on Jassa Singh wheeling his horse, dust swirling, families in background
panels.action: Jassa Singh sharply turns his horse, raising his arm toward the approaching Afghan line, while behind him women clutch children and look up in fear as the first distant thunder of hooves reaches them.

dialogue.text: “Form the circle! The Panth moves, and we move with it!”

i18n.hi: “घेरा बाँधो! पंथ चलेगा, हम उसके संग!”

panels.shot: epic overhead of a human ring around the convoy, like a shield around a core
panels.action: From high above, armed Sikh horsemen and foot soldiers are seen forming a rough but tightening ring around clusters of carts and walking families, spears and matchlocks pointed outward on all sides.

dialogue.text: Sri Gur Panth Prakash remembers what they do next: the fighters close rank around the non-combatants, turning the vahir itself into a moving fortress, a living shield that must not break.

i18n.hi: ‘श्री गुर पंथ प्रकाश’ अगला क़दम याद रखता है: जाबाज़, गैर–लड़ाकों को घेरे में लेकर क़तार कस देते हैं, वाहिर को ही चलता क़िला बना देते हैं — ज़िंदा ढाल, जो टूटनी नहीं।

panels.shot: mid-wide of Afghan cavalry charging, Sikh line bracing in distance
panels.action: Afghan horsemen surge forward at full gallop, lances lowered, while in the distance Sikh warriors plant their feet, some kneeling to aim matchlocks, others gripping long spears against the coming impact.

dialogue.text: Tahmas Khan Miskin, an Afghan voice, later notes their repeated resistance. Charge after charge meets a line that bends with the caravan’s slow stride, but does not simply scatter.

i18n.hi: अफ़ग़ान लेखक तह्मास ख़ान मिस्कीन बाद में उनकी बार–बार की जद्दोजहद लिखता है। हर हमला उस पंक्ति से टकराता है, जो काफ़िले की चाल संग झुकती है, पर बिखरती नहीं।

panels.shot: dynamic side-on shot of the cordon walking and fighting, smoke hanging low
panels.action: The Sikh defensive ring trudges forward, faces grim with strain, firing and reloading as they walk; Jassa Singh rides just inside the line, glancing back at the families and forward at the advancing Afghans.

dialogue.text: The battle becomes a march of fire. Step, fire, reload, step. Warriors die and are replaced by others from within. The shield is not static; it crawls, inch by inch, across the fields near Kup.

i18n.hi: जंग, आग में चलता मार्च बन जाती है। क़दम, गोली, भराई, क़दम। वीर गिरते हैं, उनकी जगह अंदर से और आ जाते हैं। ढाल ठहरी नहीं, रेंगती है — इंच–इंच कर के, कूप के खेतों पर।

panels.shot: somber wide of fleeing groups and collapsing carts amid distant combat
panels.action: Scattered groups of women and children run beside overloaded carts tilting in the ruts, some carts overturned; on a far ridge, mounted figures clash in a blur as smoke drifts over the scene.

dialogue.text: But even a shield of flesh cannot cover all. In the chaos of encirclement, many families are cut off. Chronicles speak of mass deaths, especially among those who cannot run as fast as fear demands.

i18n.hi: पर मांस की ढाल भी हर तरफ़ नहीं फैल सकती। घेराबंदी की अफ़रातफ़री में कितने ही ख़ानदान कट जाते हैं। तवारिख़ बड़े क़त्ल का ज़िक्र करती हैं, ख़ास कर उनका जो डर की रफ़्तार से तेज़ भाग नहीं पाए।

panels.shot: medium close of Jassa Singh pausing amid battle, eyes shadowed by grief yet firm
panels.action: Breathless and dust-streaked, Jassa Singh sits his horse amid the turmoil, his eyes dark with what he has seen; behind him, a gap has opened in the ring where fighters have fallen, and more step forward to close it.

dialogue.text: “We cannot save everyone. But the Panth must live.”

i18n.hi: “हम सबको नहीं बचा सकते। पर पंथ को ज़िंदा रहना है।”

panels.shot: wide shot of the sun sinking as the caravan still moves, Afghans regrouping at a distance
panels.action: Under a lowering winter sun, the reduced Sikh convoy continues to move in a tight cluster, while in the far background Afghan detachments pause to regroup, their horses standing heaving in place.

dialogue.text: By evening, the field around Kup and Rahira is a wasteland of abandoned loads and silent forms. The Sikh account speaks of tens of thousands lost. The exact number is unknown; the scale of loss is not.

i18n.hi: शाम तक कूप और रहीरा के आस–पास का मैदान, छोड़े बोझों और खामोश देहों का मरुस्थल है। सिख बयान दसियों हज़ार शहीद बताते हैं। ठीक गिनती नहीं, पर नुक़सान का पैमाना साफ़ है।

panels.shot: somber ground-level shot of scattered turbans and broken carts, no bodies shown
panels.action: At ground level, the viewer sees fallen turbans, discarded shoes, smashed clay pots, and broken cart wheels lying in the rutted earth, the emptiness heavy in the pale light of dawn.

dialogue.text: This day the Sikhs later name the Vadda Ghallughara, the Great Massacre. For them, it is not a tale of triumph, but of a community nearly cut down while protecting its own.

i18n.hi: इस दिन को सिख बाद में वड्डा ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰਾ — महान ਕਤਲੇਆਮ — नाम देते हैं। ये उनके लिए फ़तह नहीं, एक ऐसे समाज की कथा है जो अपनों को बचाते–बचाते लगभग काट दिया गया।

panels.shot: intimate medium of Jassa Singh in a makeshift camp, talking to a small gathered group
panels.action: In a sparse camp under the stars, with only a few remaining tents and fires, Jassa Singh sits on the ground among exhausted survivors, some with bandaged limbs, listening as he speaks calmly but with burning intensity.

dialogue.speaker: jassa_singh_ahluwalia
dialogue.text: “We count our dead. Tomorrow we count our strength.”

i18n.hi: “आज अपने गिनें। कल अपनी ताक़त गिनेंगे।”

panels.shot: montage-like wide of misls raiding and regrouping in the weeks after, implied through layered composition
panels.action: In a layered scene, one side shows Sikh horsemen riding fast toward a fortified town, another shows them gathering at a countryside shrine, and in the background farmers return cautiously to fields under the same saffron flags.

dialogue.text: Modern historians trace what happens next. Within months, the misls recover. Raids resume. Forts are tested. The Afghans move on. A massacre, meant to end the Sikhs, becomes one more scar they carry forward.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार आगे की कड़ी जोड़ते हैं। कुछ ही महीनों में मिसलें फिर सँभलती हैं। धावे लौटते हैं, क़िले फिर आज़माए जाते हैं, अफ़ग़ान आगे बढ़ जाते हैं। ये ਕਤ्लेआम, जो सिखों का अंत होना था, बस एक और ज़ख्म बन जाता है जो वो साथ लेकर चलते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Jassa Singh later, older, overlooking fields from a rise
panels.action: An older Jassa Singh stands on a low rise, looking out over green Punjabi fields and a cluster of growing town buildings, his posture straight but his face lined with remembered grief and resolve.

dialogue.text: The moving shield at Kup did not save all, but it kept a people alive. In that hard choice—protect the living, mourn the lost—Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and his age still speak to anyone who walks through ruin and must rise again.

i18n.hi: कूप की चलती ढाल सबको नहीं बचा सकी, पर एक कौम को ज़िंदा रख गई। इसी सख़्त चुनाव में — जीते को बचाना, खोए पर मातम — जੱਸा सिंह अहलूवालिया और उनका दौर आज भी हर उस शख़्स से बातें करता है जो खंडहरों से गुज़रकर फिर उठना चाहता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and the Vadda Ghallughara: a nation walks through fire
subtitle_i18n.hi: जੱਸा सिंह अहलूवालिया और वੱਡਾ ਘੱਲੂਘਾਰਾ: आग से गुज़रती कौम
